Narrative NV-024
The investigation concluded that the property manager systematically targeted tenants through illegal coercion. He initiated utility shutoffs, which were documented on internal maintenance work orders, though the field for legitimate service authorization remained blank. Subsequently, he altered the unit's locks, a fact recorded on key control logs where the supervising manager's signature line was conspicuously empty. To intimidate occupants further, he distributed threatening notices, copies of which were filed in correspondence records lacking any required legal review initials. Finally, he made the apartment uninhabitable through deliberate neglect, as noted on tenant complaint forms where the inspection date column was never filled in. To evade oversight, he falsified compliance records, a practice evident in audit summaries missing the auditor's certification block. Authorities confirmed these actions constituted intentional harassment and illegal lockouts. The manager was removed from duties, and tenants received back rent. The file closed with a recommendation for civil penalties. No further action was required, as the pattern of misconduct was irrefutable and the housing authority had successfully restored the affected units to proper, legal management standards.
